inferredCityLabelling: A city is never presented as the roll's mailing city unless the roll said it. `situsCityBasis` travels with the value: 'cad-roll' where the roll's own situsCity cell is a value, 'city-limits' where the city is the one whose limits contain the parcel and the roll's situsCity is DECLARED absent-verified. Where the basis is 'city-limits', the card's provenance gains the note 'city whose limits contain this parcel (the county roll states no situs city)', so a customer reads what the city is. An unincorporated parcel with no roll city and no cityLimits value names no city at all, and an unslated, refused, legacy-transitional or malformed situsCity rail names no city — four shapes, four tests.

fleetMemory.LESSON: A composed address is a place where three surfaces can each drop a different component and every one of them looks fine locally: the map card line, the outbound envelope address and the MCP's situs label had three separate composers and each dropped a different part. If a value has more than one composing site, the rule must live once per repo or the drift is invisible until a customer compares two surfaces. The share header was a fourth site hiding in a file whose name does not contain the word 'address'.

When a fix's predicate can be satisfied while a component is still dropped, the fix is not self-verifying. Here the ZIP rides a ledger rail the probe cannot see unless the payload carries it, so the honest closure is to make the payload REPORT what the reader served per rail (recordRailStates) and to record that map in the artifact — a measurement, not a claim.
